diagnosis.summary: order-api returns HTTP 500 on POST /orders at about 24% 5xx; Postgres reports relation "orders" does not exist. No workload or config change preceded the incident, so the likely cause is a database schema problem.

probable_cause.statement: order-api queries a Postgres table "orders" that does not exist in the database it connects to, so its requests fail with 500 errors.

supporting.statement: No new ReplicaSet or ConfigMap in sentinel-staging before the incident, so a workload or config change is unlikely to be the trigger.
Argo CD syncs before the incident changed no workload or config in sentinel-staging, which argues against a release as the cause.
Errors are confined to order-api: risk-engine shows zero 5xx and low latency, and the failing requests are POST /orders from loadgen.

missing_evidence: No 1-hour baseline values for error rate, latency or request rate, so a traffic change cannot be ruled out.
No database migration or schema history, so it is unknown why the orders table is missing or whether it was ever created in this environment.
No Postgres health, connection or database-selection details, so it is unclear whether order-api points at the wrong database or schema.
No infrastructure or node metrics, so resource causes are not assessed.
